correctness.rationale: Retain the validated correctness finding. Four distinct neighbors for every n≥5 give the stated local binary equation; four consecutive bits determine the next bit and also determine the previous bit. A primitive periodic solution cannot repeat its four-bit state inside a period, so its period is at most 16. The retained independent enumeration of every primitive binary necklace of lengths 2–16 tested the four lifted offsets with their multiplicities, recovering exactly the eleven stated words in their eight parameter rows; separate actual-graph enumeration for n=5 through 13 agreed. Each primitive word gives precisely its length in labeled shifts if and only if the period divides n. For the two (1,2) words adjacency of selected positions distinguishes them under cycle reflection as well. The newly recovered earlier infinite-graph classification independently agrees with the census after expanding the two color names, removing duplicate rotations, and sorting by their local counts.
residual_risks: The small-order enumeration alone is not the proof; the four-bit bound and all-necklace census cover all n≥5. Orbits are for translations of named classes, not arbitrary automorphism orbits of the finite graph.

originality.rationale: The exact census is covered. Parshina's 2014 general classification treats all perfect two-colorings for consecutive distances, and Lisitsyna–Parshina 2017 explicitly list all periods for distances 1 and 2, even for arbitrarily many colors. Restricting their variable-color theorem to exactly two named colors gives all eleven primitive words, including the two different five-periodic (1,2) patterns and the six-periodic balanced one. Their stated infinite/finite correspondence followed by d labeled shifts at multiples of d gives the exact counts without a new classification or substantive implication.
residual_risks: The exact overlap is supported by primary mathematical text, not by a failed query or a related many-color citation. English publisher full texts were not needed after recovering the exact Russian originals.
